metadata.description: Climate change - surface air temperature | Value 03/26 | April 2026 Release

base_case.condition: What will be the monthly global surface air temperature anomaly measured against pre-industrial levels (1850–1900) published by EU Copernicus Climate Change Service for month ending {observation.release_date}?
base_case.fsp_resolution: FSP equals the global surface air temperature value for the reference period 1850-1900 representative of the pre-industrial level for month ending {observation.reference_date} as published by the EU Copernicus Climate Change Service in their 'Surface air temperature' monthly Climate bulletin. The 1850-1900 reference period is used by UN Climate Action <https://www.un.org/en/climatechange> for monitoring the approach of global temperature to the limits specified in the COP21 Paris Agreement of 2015. Primary sources: <https://climate.copernicus.eu/climate-bulletin> for month ending {observation.release_date}; underlying data {source_name} {source_uri}. Secondary sources: 'ERA5 monthly averaged data on single levels (C3S/ECMWF)' monthly <https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means> and daily <https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/climatepulse/data/series/era5_daily_series_2t_global.csv> (daily); the Copernicus methodology for calculating the offset for the reference period 1850-1900 is described at <https://climate.copernicus.eu/climate-bulletin-about-data-and-analysis>.

edge_cases.condition: Copernicus does not publish a monthly global surface air temperature value for the reference period 1850-1900 representative of the pre-industrial level for 31 days after {observation.reference_date}
